governor noun

of a province or state

also governors, provincial governor, state governor, governor of a province, governorship, govern (a province)

classical

praeses, praesidis m./f.

Declension on Wiktionary

governor (of a province or region)

Properly a guardian or one who presides; from Augustus on, the general word for the governor of a province, whatever his rank (the jurists in the Digest; Lewis & Short). Modern Latin also uses praeses for a president (see president), so say whose governor: praeses prōvinciae.

Other words

  • rēctor prōvinciae — the ruler of a province, governor

    noun phrase: rēctor, rēctōris m. · also used · classical · Tac. Ann. 2.4; Suet. Aug. 89 (Lewis & Short, s.v. rēctor)

  • prōcōnsul, prōcōnsulis m. — proconsul: a governor with a consul’s powers

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 2.76 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    The Republican title of a former consul sent to govern a province; for a Roman governor, not a modern one.

  • gubernātor, gubernātōris m. — governor (of a colony or a modern state)

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. governor (Turselinus 1652; Way 1771, of a colonial governor of Pennsylvania); Traupman 179; Traupman 323 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically a helmsman, and so figuratively a guide of the state: custōdēs gubernātōrēsque reī pūblicae (Cic. Rab. Perd. 26; Lewis & Short). Later Latin made it the title of royal and colonial governors (Morgan–Owens).

  • prōcūrātor, prōcūrātōris m. — governor of a minor province

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. prōcūrātor: of the governors of small provinces under the emperors; Traupman 179; Traupman 323 · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • Praeses prōvinciae crās in oppidum veniet.

    The governor of the province is coming to the town tomorrow.composed

  • prōvinciae praesidēre

    to govern a provinceTraupman 179

See also province, president, rule, government.
